questions.q: Why did Bazaar move the delivery rule into a function delivery_charge()?
options: Functions run faster than if statements
So the rule is written once: change it in one place and every caller follows
Python requires every if to be in a function
To hide the code from other developers
questions.explain: Copies of a rule drift apart (the cart says free, the invoice charges ₹49). One function, many callers.

questions.q: def rupees(paise): ... and then rupees(29900). Which is the parameter and which is the argument?
options: paise is the argument, 29900 is the parameter
paise is the parameter (the name inside), 29900 is the argument (the value passed in)
questions.explain: The parameter is the blank on the form; the argument is what you fill in for this call.

questions.q: A function calculates the subtotal and ends with print(total), no return. What does subtotal = cart_subtotal(cart) store?
questions.explain: print only shows it on screen. A function without return gives back None, and later maths with None crashes.

questions.q: def line_total(price_paise, quantity=1): ... What does line_total(64900) use for quantity?
questions.explain: A parameter with a default takes that value when the caller doesn't pass one. line_total(29900, quantity=2) overrides it.

questions.q: tax is made inside gst(). After calling gst(64900), the next line runs print(tax). What happens?
options: NameError: name 'tax' is not defined, because tax was local to the function
questions.explain: Local names disappear when the function returns. Keep the result instead: tax = gst(64900).

questions.q: The error says: TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'. What's the most likely cause?
options: A value that should be a number is None, usually because some function forgot to return
questions.explain: NoneType means None. Read the traceback upwards to find which call gave back None, then add the missing return.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Why is def add(item, cart=[]) a bug?
options: The default list is made once and shared by every call, so items pile up between calls
questions.explain: Defaults are created when def runs, not on each call. Use cart=None and make a new list inside.

questions.q: (Going deeper) In def order_summary(customer, *items, **options), what is items for order_summary("Ravi", "Cotton Kurta", "Masala Box", gift_wrap=True)?
options: ('Cotton Kurta', 'Masala Box'), a tuple of the extra positional arguments
questions.explain: *items collects extra positional arguments into a tuple; **options collects extra keyword arguments into a dict.
